mark_breakdown.desc: Stating that height is continuous with reasoning

subparts.solution: The height of an emperor penguin is a numerical variable which can be measured. $\therefore$ height is a continuous variable.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Continuous variables can take any value within a range and are measured rather than counted.
step_by_step: Determine whether height is counted (discrete) or measured (continuous).
Since height can take any fractional value along a continuous scale, it is a continuous variable.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing continuous variables with discrete numerical variables.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Total sample size is found by summing all the class frequencies.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Arithmetic errors when adding multiple numbers.

mark_breakdown.desc: Correct axes, labels, and class boundaries
Correct bar heights matching class frequencies

subparts.solution: Draw a frequency histogram with penguin heights ($105$ to $135\text{ cm}$) on the horizontal axis and frequencies ($0$ to $20$) on the vertical axis.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A continuous grouped data histogram uses continuous class boundaries on the x-axis with contiguous rectangles.
step_by_step: Mark the class intervals: $105-110, 110-115, \dots, 130-135$ on the horizontal axis.
Mark frequencies on the vertical axis up to 20.
Draw bars for each interval matching heights $3, 5, 14, 19, 8, 1$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Plotting midpoints instead of full intervals as column widths.
